name: Question 7
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041015/assets/ba3d2c8719c97911d2339548f08601b07bcfe555d59dbb058a157836c45a34fe.png)

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the parabola shown above?
worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is horizontal, has its vertex at $(-4,2),$ and passes through the point $(-5,4).$

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=p{t}^{2},\,y-k=2pt,
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(-4,2),$ and so we have

$$
x+4=p{t}^{2},\,y-2=2pt.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(-5,4),$ we can substitute $x=-5$ and $y=4$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
{\begin{aligned}-1=p{t}^{2} \\ 2=2pt.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the second equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =2pt \\ 1 & =pt \\ t & =\frac{1}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the first equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & =p{(\frac{1}{p})}^{2} \\ -1 & =p\cdot \frac{1}{{p}^{2}} \\ -1 & =\frac{1}{p} \\ p & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x+4=(-1){t}^{2},\,y-2=2(-1)t,
$$

which simplify to

$$
x+4=-{t}^{2},\,y-2=-2t.
$$

Question 7

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for t∈(−∞,∞), generate the parabola shown above?

a
x+4=−t2,y−2=−2t
b
x+4=t2,y−2=t
c
x+4=−2t2,y−2=−2t
d
x−4=t2,y+2=2t
e
x−4=−t2,y+2=−2t
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The diagram shows that the parabola is horizontal, has its vertex at (−4,2), and passes through the point (−5,4).

The parametric equations of a horizontal parabola that has its vertex at (h,k) are

x−h=pt2,y−k=2pt,

where p is constant.

In our case, (h,k)=(−4,2), and so we have

x+4=pt2,y−2=2pt.

Since the parabola passes through (−5,4), we can substitute x=−5 and y=4 into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

{−1=pt22=2pt.

Solving the second equation for t, we have

2=2pt1=ptt=1p.

Substituting this into the first equation and solving for p, we get

−1=p(1p)2−1=p⋅1p2−1=1pp=−1.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

x+4=(−1)t2,y−2=2(−1)t,

which simplify to

x+4=−t2,y−2=−2t.
